stem: The primacy effect is attributed to
options: recall of information stored in long-term memory.
a type of rehearsal that improves memory for all items in a list.
recall of information still active in short-term memory.
forgetting of early items in a list as they are replaced by later items.

stem: The primacy effect (from the serial position curve experiment) is associated with ___________ memory.
Murdoch’s “remembering a list” experiment described the serial position curve and found that memory is best for ___________ of a list.
options: both the first and last words

stem: When investigating the serial position curve, delaying the memory test for 30 seconds
options: has no effect on the curve.
increases both the primacy and the recency effects.

stem: Regarding free recall of a list of items, which of the following will most likely cause the recency effect to disappear by preventing rehearsal?
options: Presenting the stimulus list at a slower pace
Counting backward for 30 seconds before recall
Using a very long list (greater than 30 items at one item per second)

stem: The recency effect occurs when participants are asked to recall a list of words. One way to eliminate the recency effect is to
options: have participants say “la, la, la” while studying the list.
have participants count backwards for 30 seconds after hearing the last word of the list.
have participants see the words on a screen, rather than hear them.

stem: The predominant type of coding in long-term memory is
This multiple-choice question is an example of a ___________ test.

Lamar has just gotten a new job and is attending a company party where he will meet his colleagues for the first time. His boss escorts him around to small groups to introduce him. At the first group, Lamar meets four people and is told only their first names. The same thing happens with a second group and a third group. At the fourth group, Lamar is told their names and that one of the women in the group is the company accountant. A little while later, Lamar realizes that he only remembers the names of the people in the first group, though he also remembers the profession of the last woman he met (the accountant). Lamar’s experience demonstrates
options: a build-up and release of proactive interference.

stem: Wickens et al.’s “fruit, meat, and professions” experiment failed to show a release from proactive interference in the “fruit” group because
options: the stimulus category remained the same.
the response task remained the same.

stem: In which of the following examples of two different brain-injured patients (Tom and Tim) is a double dissociation demonstrated?
options: Both Tom and Tim have good episodic memory but poor semantic memory.
Tom and Tim both show deficits in episodic and semantic memory.
Tom has good semantic memory and poor episodic memory, while Tim has good episodic memory but poor semantic memory.
Both Tom and Tim have good semantic memory but poor episodic memory.

stem: The dramatic case of patient H.M. clearly illustrates that ___________ is crucial for the formation of long-term memories.

Your book discusses the memory functioning of patient H.M. who underwent brain surgery to relieve severe epileptic seizures. H.M.’s case has been extremely informative to psychologists by demonstrating that
options: long-term memory can operate normally while short-term memory is impaired.
impairment of one memory system (long-term or short-term) necessarily leads to deficits in the functioning of the other.
a double dissociation exists for short-term and long-term memory.
short-term memory can operate normally while long-term memory is impaired.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a conclusion from the case of H.M., who had an operation to help alleviate his epileptic seizures?
options: The hippocampus is necessary for forming new long-term memories.
Short-term and long-term memories are controlled by different mechanisms.
Short-term and long-term memories can operate independently of each other.
Long-term memories are unaffected by damage to the hippocampus.

stem: Neuropsychological evidence indicates that short- and long-term memories probably
options: represent different aspects of the same mechanism.
are caused by different mechanisms that depend upon each other.
both rely most heavily on a semantic coding mechanism.
are caused by different mechanisms that act independently.

stem: ___________ memories are those that we are not aware of.
Explicit memory is to ___________ as implicit memory is to ___________.
Which of the following is NOT an example of an implicit memory?
___________ memories are to experiences as ___________ memories are to facts.
According to Tulving, the defining property of the experience of episodic memory is that
options: it always corresponds to events from our past that actually happened.
it accesses knowledge about the world that does not have to be tied to any specific personal experience.
it involves both explicit and implicit memories.

stem: Which of the following is an example of a semantic memory?
options: I remember my earth science teacher telling me how volcanoes erupt.
I remember seeing a volcano erupt in Hawaii last summer.
I remember the big island of Hawaii has many active volcanoes.
I remember “volcano” was the first word on the list Juan read to me.

stem: The following statement represents what kind of memory? “The Beatles stopped making music together as a group in the early 1970s.”
“I remember being really excited last year, when my college team won the national championship in basketball.” This statement is an example of ___________ memory.

K.C., who was injured in a motorcycle accident, remembers facts like the difference between a strike and a spare in bowling, but he is unaware of experiencing things like hearing about the circumstances of his brother’s death, which occurred two years before the accident. His memory behavior suggests
options: intact semantic memory but defective episodic memory.
intact procedural memory but defective semantic memory.
intact episodic memory but defective semantic memory.
intact episodic memory but defective procedural memory.

stem: Your text describes an “Italian woman” who, after an attack of encephalitis, had difficulty remembering people or facts she knew before. She could, however, remember her life events and daily tasks. Her memory behavior reflects
options: intact semantic memory but defective episodic memory.
intact procedural memory but defective episodic memory.
intact episodic memory but defective semantic memory.
intact episodic memory but defective procedural memory.

stem: A patient with impaired episodic memory would most likely have the greatest difficulty in
options: remembering the meaning of some words.
recalling where to find eating utensils in the kitchen.

stem: Which of the following statements is the most accurate with regard to autobiographical memories?
options: When autobiographical memories are impaired, their episodic content will block access to related semantic content.
Autobiographical memories can involve both episodic and semantic content.
Autobiographical memories are highly accurate from as early as 3 years of age.
It is not possible to have an autobiographical memory that has only semantic or episodic content.

stem: Your text discusses how episodic and semantic memories are interconnected. This discussion revealed that when we experience events,
options: episodic memory for events lasts longer than semantic memory for the events.
the knowledge that makes up semantic memories is initially attained through a personal experience based in episodic memory.
semantic and episodic memories about events tend to last about the same length of time in our memory.
semantic memory of events is enhanced when it is not interfered with by associated episodic memories.

stem: Ming is taking a memory test. She is more likely to recall the name of a popular singer if she had
options: just read about the singer in a magazine.
just seen the singer on TV.
recently seen the singer on TV and read about the singer in a magazine.
attended the singer’s concert last year with her boyfriend.

stem: One of the defining characteristics of implicit memory is that
options: it always leads to episodic memory for events.
it is enhanced by the self-reference effect.
people are not conscious they are using it.
people use it strategically to enhance memory for events.

stem: Lucille is teaching Kendra how to play racquetball. She explains how to hold the racquet, how to stand, and how to make effective shots. These learned skills that Lucille has acquired are an example of ___________ memory.
A man suffering from Korsakoff’s syndrome would be able to perform which of the following activities without difficulty?
options: Following a story in a book
Remembering what he needs to buy when he gets to the grocery store
Recognizing people he has recently met
Identifying a photograph of his childhood home

stem: Memory enhancement due to repetition priming is a result of the test stimulus being
options: the same as or resembling the priming stimulus.
similar in meaning to the priming stimulus.
different in meaning from the priming stimulus.

stem: Work with brain-injured patients reveals that ___________ memory does not depend on conscious memory.
Which of the following involves procedural memory?
options: Knowing how it feels to be scared
Knowing how an automobile engine works
Reading a sentence in a book

stem: The propaganda effect demonstrates that we evaluate familiar statements as being true
options: only when we are aware we’ve seen them before.
simply because we have been exposed to them before.
only when we agree with them.
unless we are told explicitly that the statements are false.

stem: Which of the following is most closely associated with implicit memory?
Why is classical conditioning considered a form of implicit memory?
options: Because learning the association between the neutral and conditioned stimulus requires effort.
Because it is based on motor skills similar to procedural memory.
Because it involves learning an association without being aware of the reasons behind it.
Because it usually involves memory for the episode in which it occurred.

According to Tulving, an episodic memory is distinguished by the process of ________ it.

Procedural memories are also known as ________ memories.
